newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Foreign deal fuels Avgold despite poor Q2.
newsitem.headline: Foreign deal fuels Avgold despite poor Q2.

text.p: A foreign trade of 400,000 shares pushed South African mining company Avgold Ltd nearly five percent higher to 440 cents on Wednesday, dealers said.
The share's rise was despite disappointing second quarter gold results announced on Tuesday.
Brokers Fleming Martin confirmed they had made the deal.
"It was a foreign trade. Not an asset swap, just a normal deal," one Fleming Martin trader said.
By 0850 GMT Avgold was up 10 cents at 430 cents, off its morning best of 440 cents, in a volume of 506,200 shares worth over two million rand.
Dealers said the foreign trade was made at 430 cents.
Avgold was one of the few South African gold shares trading on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange that was not weaker on Wednesday, dulled by a bullion price shaky at $326 an ounce.

Avgold fell into a net loss of 1.1 million rand in the second quarter from a one million rand profit in the preceding quarter. It also announced that the weak bullion price had forced it to shorten the life of its Loraine division to two years from a previously expected three years.
